meta.title: Environment and climate
meta.question: Should the environment come before economic growth?
meta.measure: Average position on the environment and the climate, from 0 (environment first) to 10 (growth first)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on protecting the environment, spending on it, climate change and climate policy, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: Do you approve or disapprove of the ecology or nature protection movement?
If we want to combat unemployment, we shall just have to accept environmental problems
I would give part of my income if I were certain the money would be used to prevent environmental pollution
items.notes: European Values Study 1990, 1999, 2008 (3 surveys). 2017 adds a middle category and is EVS_ENV_INCOME_5.

items.wording: Protecting the environment and fighting pollution is less urgent than often suggested
I would agree to an increase in taxes if the extra money were used to prevent environmental pollution
Which do you agree with more: the environment first, or industry first? (can't choose = 5)
items.notes: Consolidation of Democracy in CEE, January 1991 and March 2000 (2 surveys). 'Can't choose' exists only in 2000.

items.wording: Are we spending too much, too little or about the right amount on protecting the environment?
Would you be willing to accept cuts in your standard of living to protect the environment?
We worry too much about the future of the environment and not enough about prices and jobs today (agree-disagree)
Would you be willing to pay much higher taxes to protect the environment?
Protecting the environment (0) or economic growth and creating jobs (10) should be given priority
items.notes: World Values Survey 1997, 2005, 2012 (3 surveys). 2005's 'other answer' is no position.

items.wording: I would buy things at 20% higher than usual prices if it would help to protect the environment
I would agree to an increase in taxes if the extra money were used to prevent environmental pollution
Should it be the government's responsibility to impose strict laws to make industry do less damage to the environment?
Government spending on the environment: much more ... much less
How far is the state of the natural environment in Poland a cause of worry to you?
items.notes: CBOS 1999-07, 2000-09, 2006-06, 2008-05, 2011-02, 2014-11, 2016-02 (7 surveys). Could join GAL-TAN with exclusions for the waves before 2016.

items.wording: Important to care for nature and the environment: how much like you is this person?
The state should care more about environmental protection
I would give part of my income if I were certain the money would be used to prevent environmental pollution
How serious a problem is global warming or the greenhouse effect for the world as a whole?
Is climate change or global warming caused by the greenhouse effect a very serious problem ... of no importance?
How far is the state of the natural environment on Earth a cause of worry to you?
No costly steps until we are sure climate change is a problem (10); deal with it gradually (5); a serious and urgent problem to act on now even at high cost (0)
Protecting the environment should be a priority (statement battery; check the exact wording in the questionnaires)
items.notes: Eurobarometer 2006, 2008, 2009 x2, 2012 (5 surveys). Asked of one split-ballot half in each. Two copies in 2008-09 (the second for the Turkish Cypriot community); the first is used.

items.wording: Protecting the environment should be given priority, even if it causes slower economic growth and some loss of jobs
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2007, 2009, 2010 (3 surveys; not asked in Poland in 2002 and 2008).

items.wording: Is global warming a very serious problem, somewhat serious, not too serious, or not a problem?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2007, 2008, 2009 (3 surveys). From 2010 the wording is 'global climate change' (PEW_CLIMATE_SERIOUS).

items.wording: The seriousness of climate change has been exaggerated
How serious a problem is climate change at this moment? (1 not at all serious ... 10 extremely serious)
items.notes: Eurobarometer 2008, 2009 x2, 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021 (9 surveys). 2008 was a split ballot (half sample). 2025 uses four points (EB_CLIMATE_SERIOUS_4). Could join GAL-TAN with exclusions for pre-2016 waves.

items.wording: If things continue on their present course, we will soon experience a major environmental catastrophe
The balance of nature is strong enough to cope with the impacts of modern industrial nations
People should be willing to pay higher prices in order to address global climate change
So-called global warming is above all a business for certain interests
Climate change is one of the greatest threats to civilisation (1) ... there is no such thing as climate change (5)
items.notes: CBOS 2009-12, 2014-11, 2016-02 (3 surveys). Could join GAL-TAN with exclusions for 2009 and 2014.

items.wording: What is your own view of climate change? One of the greatest threats to civilisation (0) ... some threat, one of many ... no significant threat ... not dangerous at all ... no such thing exists (10)
items.notes: CBOS: microdata December 2009, November 2014, April 2016; reports November 2018, May 2021, November 2025.

items.wording: It is not certain that the climate is changing at all
Is global climate change a very serious problem, somewhat serious, not too serious, or not a problem?
Is the EU 2020 objective of cutting greenhouse gases by 20% too ambitious (10), about right (5) or too modest (0)?
Is the EU 2020 objective of raising renewable energy to 20% too ambitious (10), about right (5) or too modest (0)?
Taxation should be based more on how much energy people use, to fight climate change
Is global climate change a major threat, a minor threat or not a threat to the country?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2013, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2022, 2025 (6 surveys; 2025 by telephone, split off as _TEL). Could join GAL-TAN with an exclusion for 2013 (see notes).

items.wording: How important is it that the government sets targets to increase renewable energy?
items.notes: Eurobarometer 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021 (5 surveys). Could join GAL-TAN with exclusions for 2013 and 2015.

items.wording: How concerned are you about global climate change?
Favour banning the least energy-efficient household appliances to reduce climate change
Is climate change caused by natural processes, human activity or both?
items.notes: European Social Survey 2016, 2021 and 2023; 'I don't think climate change is happening' left out.

items.wording: To what extent do you feel a personal responsibility to try to reduce climate change?
Favour increasing taxes on fossil fuels to reduce climate change
Favour subsidising renewable energy to reduce climate change
How worried are you about climate change?
items.notes: European Social Survey 2016, 2021 and 2023; those who think the climate is not changing are not asked.

items.wording: More public financial support should go to the transition to clean energy even if it means cutting subsidies for fossil fuels
How important is protecting the environment to you personally?
Many of the claims about environmental threats are exaggerated
Protecting the environment should be given priority, even if it causes slower growth and some loss of jobs (0), or economic growth and creating jobs should be the top priority (10)?
items.notes: European Values Study 2017 (1 survey). Same question as WVS_ENV_GROWTH.

items.wording: As EVS_ENV_INCOME_4, five points
There are more important things to do in life than protect the environment
Greenhouse gas emissions should be reduced to a minimum to make the EU economy climate-neutral by 2050
Environmental protection should take priority even at the cost of growth (0) ... growth even at the cost of the environment (10)
items.notes: European Election Study 2019 (1 survey); the format of EES 2024's EES_CLIMATE.

items.wording: Climate change and pollution are the most pressing problem of contemporary Poland vs not an important problem, 1-7
After the epidemic, should financial priority go to fighting climate change and protecting the environment (0) or to supporting business and the economy (10)?
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker wave 7 (1 online survey).

items.wording: Climate change and pollution are the most pressing problem in Poland today (1) ... are not an important problem, others matter far more (7)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 9, 11, 13 (3 online surveys). The PGSW_CLIMATE wording.

items.wording: Warming is caused by normal natural cycles (1) ... almost entirely by human activity (5)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 11 and 13 (2 online surveys).

items.wording: Protecting the environment and the climate matters more than growth and prosperity (1) ... growth matters more (5)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 11 and 13 (2 online surveys).

items.wording: Protecting the environment, the climate and animals matters, but most people have become hysterical and exaggerate
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker waves 11, 13 (2 online surveys).

items.wording: What is your own view of climate change? One of the greatest threats to civilisation (0) ... some threat, one of many ... no significant threat ... not dangerous at all ... no such thing exists (10)
items.notes: CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI or CAWI, the respondent's choice) from APiW 359 (May-June 2020), so a question of its own.

items.wording: Poland should move away from coal (1) vs use coal as long as possible (7)
items.notes: CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI or CAWI, the respondent's choice) from APiW 359 (May-June 2020), so a question of its own.

items.wording: Is climate change caused by natural processes, human activity or both?
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: To what extent do you feel a personal responsibility to try to reduce climate change?
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: How worried are you about climate change?
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: How important is making choices that help reduce the effects of global climate change for being a good member of society?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes 2022 (1 survey; 2025's version was not asked in Poland).

items.wording: The EU should invest massively in renewable energies such as wind and solar power
Protecting the environment and the climate is more important (1) vs ensuring economic growth and prosperity is more important (5)
As above, round 11's version
Limiting climate change should take priority (0) vs economic growth should take priority (10)
Is climate change a very serious, fairly serious, not very serious or not at all serious problem?
Is global climate change a major threat, a minor threat or not a threat to the country?
items.notes: Pew spring 2025: by telephone in Poland, where every earlier wave was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: To cut air pollution, cities should restrict combustion vehicles (1) ... the state should not favour electric vehicles (7)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online surveys May and December 2025 (2 surveys).

items.wording: Climate change and pollution, as above, 1-7
Protecting nature matters more, even if a road or factory must be given up (1) ... economic development matters more (7)
items.notes: FNW SWPS online survey May 2026 (1 survey).
